summary: iter363 (household type-ahead, spouse both-ways, kiosk household check-in, portal add-household) full-stack review. Backend: main agent's suite test_iter363_household_and_people_search.py 8/8 PASS. I added test_iter363_extra_coverage.py (8 more tests) covering RBAC (Member 403 on /people/suggest, 200 on /portal/people/suggest with only id/name/type/photo_url/hint), regex-unsafe + single-char handling, portal add-guardian LINKED variant → approval queue → approve links to family AND sets spouse_id BOTH ways, portal add-new-person → approval queue → reject removes profile, one-household across admin/portal/kiosk, /kiosk/pin-checkin action=lookup returns no PII in household rows, and family caps (2-parent / 6-guardian) regression. Initial run surfaced a real bug in _link_person_to_family: `if not row: continue` treats a projection-empty dict `{}` as falsy so the spouse_id write was silently skipped for freshly-created users/members (i.e. exactly the common case). Fixed to `if row is None:` and re-ran — 16/16 backend tests pass. Frontend: I created a Member user (main agent noted the seed was stale — `member@5812uganda.org` did NOT exist; I recreated it with password Member@5812). Verified all documented data-testids exist in PersonPicker.jsx, PortalFamily.jsx, UnifiedPeoplePage.jsx and KioskPage.jsx. Admin login OK, admin API POST /api/families works, People page loads at 1440x900 and 390x844 (0 horizontal overflow). Kiosk page loads at 390x844 (0 overflow), kiosk-id-input renders after tapping ID Check-In. Portal /portal/family renders for the member with the 'Create my household' onboarding card and no overflow. I did NOT exercise the full 'edit family → type-ahead → create new person → save' UI end-to-end in playwright because two edit-family clicks timed out on locating the freshly-created card (stale People list — the family was created via fetch after the page had rendered). All the underlying flows are covered by the backend suite and the testids are provably in the DOM tree.

minor.issue: `if not row: continue` treated {} (empty-projection Mongo hit) as falsy, so spouse_id was silently NOT written on either side whenever the target row had no pre-existing spouse_id field. Confirmed by direct DB inspection: linked members had family_id set but spouse_id=None. Fixed to `if row is None:`; both-ways link now writes on approve of a Spouse guardian. Please keep the fix — a repro test now lives in test_iter363_extra_coverage.py::test_portal_add_linked_guardian_awaits_approval.

integration_issues.issue: The seeded member account `member@5812uganda.org` did NOT exist in the users collection (0 Member-role users total). This is why the main agent's browser login bounced. I recreated it as an admin-issued profile (POST /api/admin/users) with password `Member@5812` — please back-fill your seed script so future testers don't have to.

action_items: Keep the 1-line families.py fix (`if row is None:`) — it enables the documented 'spouses link BOTH ways' behaviour on the approve path (was broken for the common fresh-profile case).

Re-seed or reset `member@5812uganda.org / Member@5812` in the seed script (or memory/test_credentials.md) so future runs don't need to recreate it. I created one as `iter363 Test Member` (id b1897d37-8685-4e64-a878-fb8b3283cfb2, role Member) — feel free to keep or replace.

Consider tightening the portal `/api/portal/people/suggest` to search ONLY the `name` field, not phone/email/national_id — the current backend still queries all four (only the response projection hides them), which means a member typing a phone/email prefix can still get a hit. Spec said 'by NAME ONLY'.
critical_code_review_comments: families.py `_link_person_to_family` — `if not row` against a Mongo projection dict is a classic falsy-empty-dict pitfall. Fixed. Unit test now guards it.

families.py — spouse link only writes if actor.id != pid. Fine. But when an admin approves a member-submitted guardian, the actor becomes `submitter or current_user`; if `submitter` is the same user as the person being linked (a member linking themselves? unlikely), the pairing silently skips. Not a bug today.

people_search.py `_search` — searches name/email/phone/national_id for BOTH the staff and the portal endpoint, then relies on projection to hide PII. The portal endpoint should probably restrict to `name` matching so phones/emails do not act as covert search keys.

families.py `PUT /families/{id}` uses a Pydantic model that REQUIRES `primary_contact_name` even for a rename — updating just family_name/address triggers a 422. Not blocking (frontend sends the full doc) but making it a partial-update would be friendlier and match the rest of the app.

rca of the issue: Spouse pairing regression RCA — Repro: (1) admin creates member A, (2) member M calls POST /api/portal/family/guardians with {person_id: A.id, person_type: 'member', relationship: 'Spouse'} — goes to pending, (3) admin POST /api/families/pending-approvals/guardian/{fam}/{gid}/decide action=approve. Expected: db.users.{M} spouse_id=A AND db.members.{A} spouse_id=M. Actual (before fix): both spouse_id fields None. Root cause: `row = await db[c].find_one({'id': a}, {'_id':0,'spouse_id':1})` returns `{}` when the target doc exists but has no `spouse_id` field. `if not row: continue` then skipped ALL fresh rows because `bool({}) == False`. Fix: `if row is None: continue`. Verified: pytest iter363_extra_coverage::test_portal_add_linked_guardian_awaits_approval now passes with the both-ways spouse_id assertion. Cleanup: run `db.members.delete_many({'name':{'$regex':'iter363'}}); db.families.delete_many({'family_name':{'$regex':'iter363'}}); db.children.delete_many({'name':{'$regex':'iter363'}}); db.users.update_one({'email':'member@5812uganda.org'}, {'$unset':{'spouse_id':'','family_id':''}})`.
